731.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
731.text:
Assertion : Extraction of iron metal from iron oxide ore is carried out by heating with coke. 
Reason : The reaction $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_{3(s)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}_{(s)}+3 / 2 \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}$ is a spontaneous process.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
731.sol:
Extraction of iron metal from iron oxide ore is carried out by heating with coke and flux (calcium carbonate). Flux is a slag forming substance. It converts infusible impurities into fusible slag.
The reaction : $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_{3(s)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}_{(s)}+3 / 2 \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}$ is not a spontaneous process. $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ is converted to $\mathrm{FeO}$ at about $400^{\circ} \mathrm{C} . \mathrm{FeO}$ is converted to $\mathrm{Fe}$ at about $800^{\circ} \mathrm{C}-1000^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$

2216.sol: The environmental factors which can check the growth of population size constitute the environmental resistance. These include predators, food, water, nesting sites, similar competitors, etc. All living things tend to reproduce until the point at which their environment becomes a limiting factor. 2221.text: Keystone species deserve protection because these

indicate presence of certain minerals in the soil
have become rare due to overexploitation

2221.sol: Keystone species is a species which has significant and disproportionately large influence on the community removal or decrease in number of keystone species causes disruption in structure and function of community. For example in intertidal regions star fish feeds on mussels. Removal of star fish leads to dominance of mussels that excludes algae and browsing species. In tropical rain forests fig functions as keystone species as they provide fruit to a number of animals during the period of food scarcity.

5208.subject: Chemistry
5208.text: If two liquids A and B form a minimum boiling azeotrope at some specific composition, then which statement among the following is correct?
options: A-B molecular interactions are stronger than A-A and B-B interactions.
The total vapour pressure of the mixture is greater than that corresponding to an ideal solution.
There is a slight decrease in volume when the two components are mixed.
5208.sol:
Minimum Boiling Azeotropes :-

Non-ideal solutions showing large positive deviation from Raoult's law form minimum boiling azeotropes which boil at temperature lower than boiling point of its components $' A '$ and $' B '$, e.g., water and benzene, chloroform and methanol.

The Minimum Boiling Azeotropes has the $A - B$ molecular interactions are weaker than $A - A$ and $B - B$ interactions. They has the total vapour pressure of the mixture is greater than that corresponding to an ideal solution. There is a slight increase in volume when the two components are mixed. ${ΔH}_{mix}$ will have positive value.

Hence, the correct statement is that the total vapour pressure of the mixture is greater than that corresponding to an ideal solution.

5266.sol:
From Rault’s law for non-volatile solute, we know that
$\frac{p^{{}^{\circ}}-p_s}{p^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{n_2}{n_1+n_2}$
For dilute solution, relative lowering of vapour pressure,
$\begin{aligned}
& n_2=\frac{18}{180}=0.1 \\
& n_1=\frac{90}{18}=5 \\
& \frac{p^{{}^{\circ}}-p_s}{p^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{0.1}{5}=0.02
\end{aligned}$

$\therefore \quad i=\frac{3}{1}=3=\frac{M_c}{M_o}$
(where, $M_c=$ calculated molar mass and $M_o=$ observed molar mass)
$\begin{array}{ll} & 3=\frac{M_c}{M_o} \\ \text{ or } & M_o=\frac{M_c}{3} \\ \text{ i.e., } \quad & M_o < M_c\end{array}$
or observed molecular mass of $\mathrm{BaCl}_2$ is less than the calculated molecular mass.

& m_2=\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{(0,0)}=\frac{-5}{2}\\
& m_1 \times m_2=\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{-5}{2}=-1
\end{aligned}$ The $two lines are perpendicular i.e. angle between them is \pi / 2$.

10748.text: Two integers are drawn at random from the set $\{5,6,.., \ldots 35\}$. What is the probability that their difference is odd?
10748.sol:
Two integers are drawn from $\{5,6, \ldots \ldots, 35\}$
Given, integer are 31
Total ways of choosing 2 integer from 31 integers ={ }^{31} C_2 Two integer difference will be odd only when one is even and other is odd.
Let $ A$ be the event of selecting two integers whose difference is odd.
Now, $P(A)+P(\bar{A})=1P(\bar{A})=$ Probability of selecting two integers whose difference is not odd.
Case I When two integers are even.
Total ways of choosing 2 integer (even) from 15 even integers $={ }^{15} C_2$
Case II When two integers are odd Total ways $={ }^{16} C_2 \begin{aligned}$ P(\bar{A}) & =$\frac{{ }^{15} C_2+{ }^{16} C_2}{{ }^{31} C_2}=\frac{\frac{15 \times 14}{2}+\frac{16 \times 15}{2}}{\frac{31 \times 30}{2}}$\\
P \overline{(A}) & =$\frac{(15 \times 14)+(16 \times 15)}{31 \times 30}$\\
& =$\frac{14+16}{31 \times 2}=\frac{30}{2 \times 31}=\frac{15}{31}$\\
\therefore \quad P(A) & =1-P(\bar{A})=1-$\frac{15}{31}=\frac{31-15}{31}=\frac{16}{31}
\end{aligned}$

Taking \(\log\) on the both sides, we get
\$(\begin{aligned}
\ln$\frac{1}{5}$$& =$\ln$\left($\frac{1}{2}$\right)$^{$\frac{n}{138.6}} \Rightarrow $\ln$\frac{1}{5}=\frac{n}{138.6} \ln$$\$left($\frac{1}{2}$\right)$\\
\ln 5  =\frac{n}{138.6} \ln2 \\
n & =138.6 \times $\frac{$\ln 5}{\ln$ 2}$ \quad \left[\begin{array}{l}\because \ln5=1.61 \\ \ln 2=0.693\end{array}$\right]\\
n & =138.6 $\times $\frac{1.61}{0.693} \Rightarrown=$322 $\text{ days }$
\end{aligned}$\)

Two cars are moving towards each other at the speed of $50 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$. If one of the cars blows a horn at a frequency of $250 \mathrm{ Hz}$, the wave length of the sound perceived by the driver of the other car is

$\therefore \quad v_s=50 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s} \Rightarrow v_0=-50 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$
Frequency of horn blown by the source car,
$v=250 \mathrm{ Hz}$
According to Doppler's effect, frequency heared by another car $v$ ' is given as
$v^{\prime}=\frac{v-v_0}{v-v_s} \times v=\frac{350-(-50)}{350-50} \times 250\therefore(v=$ speed of sound $=350 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s})=\frac{400 \times 250}{300} \Rightarrow v^{\prime}=\frac{100}{3} \mathrm{ Hz}$
Wavelength of heard sound,
$\lambda^{\prime}=\frac{v}{v^{\prime}}=\frac{350}{1000 / 3}=\frac{1050}{1000}=1.05 \mathrm{ m}=105 \mathrm{ cm}$

$⇒ P\left(C\right) + P\left(G\right) + P\left(K\right) = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{3} + P\left(K\right) = 1$

$∴ P\left(K\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Also, $P\left(\dfrac{A}{K}\right) = 1,$ for if the examinee knows, he/she will correctly answer it and $P\left(\dfrac{A}{G}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4},$

since there are four choices.

Now, total probability& $P\left(A\right) = P\left(G\right)P\left(\dfrac{A}{G}\right) + P \left(C\right)P \left(\dfrac{A}{C}\right) + +P\left(K\right)P\left(\dfrac{A}{K}\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{3} \cdot \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{6} \cdot \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot1$

$= \dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{1}{48} + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{4 + 1 + 24}{48} = \dfrac{29}{48}$

Now, $P\left(\dfrac{K}{A}\right) = \dfrac{P\left(K\right)P\left(\dfrac{A}{K}\right)}{P\left(A\right)}$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 1}{2948} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{48}{29} = \dfrac{24}{29}$

20386.subject: Chemistry
20386.text: Identify the Alkane (molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_8 \mathrm{H}_{18}$ ) which yields only a single monochloride on Chlorination in the presence of sunlight.
20386.sol:
The formation of only a single monochloride upon chlorination implies that all hydrogen atoms in the alkane molecule are equivalent. This means the molecule must possess a high degree of symmetry such that replacing any hydrogen atom with a chlorine atom results in the same product.

Analyzing the options:

2,4-Dimethylhexane has multiple types of hydrogen atoms (primary, secondary, and tertiary), leading to multiple monochlorinated isomers.

3,4-Dimethylhexane also has multiple types of hydrogen atoms, leading to multiple monochlorinated isomers.

2,2,3,3-Tetramethylbutane has a structure where all 18 hydrogen atoms are equivalent. Specifically, it consists of two tert-butyl groups connected by a central C-C bond. Each of the four methyl groups attached to the quaternary carbons is equivalent, and there are no other types of hydrogens. Thus, chlorination yields only one monochloride, 1-chloro-2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane.

2,2,4-Trimethylpentane (isooctane) has several distinct types of hydrogen atoms (primary, secondary, and tertiary), leading to multiple monochlorinated products.

Therefore, 2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane is the correct alkane.

Answer: 2, 2, 3, 3-Tetramethylbutane

20547.subject: Chemistry
20547.text:
Which one of the following options represents the decreasing order of oxidation number of the central atom in:
$\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-}, \mathrm{CrO}_2^{-}, \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}, \mathrm{BrO}_3^{-}$
20547.sol:
For $\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}$: Let the oxidation number of Cr be $x$. Then $2x + 7(-2) = -2$, which gives $2x = 12$, so $x = +6$.

For $\mathrm{CrO}_{2}^{-}$: Let the oxidation number of Cr be $x$. Then $x + 2(-2) = -1$, which gives $x - 4 = -1$, so $x = +3$.

For $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}$: Let the oxidation number of Mn be $x$. Then $x + 4(-2) = -1$, which gives $x - 8 = -1$, so $x = +7$.

For $\mathrm{BrO}_{3}^{-}$: Let the oxidation number of Br be $x$. Then $x + 3(-2) = -1$, which gives $x - 6 = -1$, so $x = +5$.

Comparing the oxidation numbers: $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-} (+7) > \mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-} (+6) > \mathrm{BrO}_{3}^{-} (+5) > \mathrm{CrO}_{2}^{-} (+3)$.

Answer: $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-} > \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-} > \mathrm{BrO}_3^{-} > \mathrm{CrO}_2^{-}$

20680.subject: Chemistry
20680.text: Under which of the following condition, the gases does not follow Henry's law?
options: When gases are placed under high temperature.
When the molecules of the system are in equilibrium state.
When gases are placed under extremely high pressure.
20680.sol:
Henry's law states that the mass of a gas dissolved in a given volume of solvent is directly proportional to the pressure of the gas in equilibrium with the liquid at a constant temperature. The law is valid only under specific conditions: the pressure should be low, the temperature should not be too low, and the gas should not undergo any chemical reaction with the solvent.

At extremely high pressures, the gas molecules are packed closely together, leading to significant intermolecular forces and deviations from ideal gas behavior. Consequently, the solubility does not follow the linear relationship predicted by Henry's law.

Therefore, gases do not follow Henry's law when placed under extremely high pressure.

Answer: When gases are placed under extremely high pressure.

21173.subject: Mathematics
21173.text: $\text{ The modulus of the following complex number } \dfrac{1+i}{1-i}-\dfrac{1-i}{1+i} \text{$ is }
21173.sol:
Let $z = \dfrac{1+i}{1-i} - \dfrac{1-i}{1+i}$.

Simplify the first term by multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator $(1+i)$:
$\dfrac{1+i}{1-i} = \dfrac{(1+i)(1+i)}{(1-i)(1+i)} = \dfrac{1 + 2i + i^2}{1^2 - i^2} = \dfrac{1 + 2i - 1}{1 + 1} = \dfrac{2i}{2} = i$.

Simplify the second term by multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator $(1-i)$:
$\dfrac{1-i}{1+i} = \dfrac{(1-i)(1-i)}{(1+i)(1-i)} = \dfrac{1 - 2i + i^2}{1^2 - i^2} = \dfrac{1 - 2i - 1}{1 + 1} = \dfrac{-2i}{2} = -i$.

Substitute these values back into the expression for $z$:
$z = i - (-i) = i + i = 2i$.

The modulus of $z$ is $|z| = |2i| = \sqrt{0^2 + 2^2} = 2$.

Answer: 2

21891.subject: Mathematics
21891.text:
Two numbers are selected at random from integers 1 to 9.
If their sum is even, what is the probability that both the numbers are odd?
21891.sol:
The set of integers is $S = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9\}$. The number of odd integers is $5$ (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and the number of even integers is $4$ (2, 4, 6, 8).

The total number of ways to select two distinct numbers from 9 is $^{9}C_{2} = \dfrac{9 \times 8}{2} = 36$.

The sum of two numbers is even if both are odd or both are even. The number of ways to select two odd numbers is $^{5}C_{2} = \dfrac{5 \times 4}{2} = 10$. The number of ways to select two even numbers is $^{4}C_{2} = \dfrac{4 \times 3}{2} = 6$.

The total number of ways to have an even sum is $10 + 6 = 16$.

Let $A$ be the event that both numbers are odd and $E$ be the event that the sum is even. We want to find $P(A|E) = \dfrac{P(A \cap E)}{P(E)}$. Since $A \subset E$, $P(A \cap E) = P(A) = \dfrac{10}{36}$.

$P(E) = \dfrac{16}{36}$.

Therefore, $P(A|E) = \dfrac{10/36}{16/36} = \dfrac{10}{16} = \dfrac{5}{8}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{8}$

22579.subject: Physics
22579.text: The resistance of the conductor is $\sqrt{3} \Omega the angle made by the V-I graph with the voltage axis is \theta$
22579.sol:
The resistance $R$ of a conductor is given by the slope of the $V-I$ graph, where $V$ is on the y-axis and $I$ is on the x-axis. Thus, $R = \dfrac{V}{I} = \tan(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is the angle made with the current axis (x-axis).

The problem states that the angle made with the voltage axis (y-axis) is $\theta$. Therefore, the angle made with the current axis is $\phi = 90^{{}^{\circ}} - \theta$.

Given $R = \sqrt{3} \Omega$, we have $\tan(\phi) = \sqrt{3}$.

Since $\tan(60^{{}^{\circ}}) = \sqrt{3}$, it follows that $\phi = 60^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Substituting $\phi = 90^{{}^{\circ}} - \theta$, we get $60^{{}^{\circ}} = 90^{{}^{\circ}} - \theta$, which implies $\theta = 30^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Answer: $\theta=30^{{}^{\circ}}$

In insulators and semiconductors at $0\text{ K}$, the conduction band is completely empty, making option A incorrect.

24044.subject: Chemistry
24044.text: Which one is an INCORRECT statement with regard to the following reaction?
options: The reaction rate decreases upon changing the solvent from ethyl alcohol to 1:1 mixture of ethyl alcohol and water.
The reaction rate does not change upon increasing the concentration of hydroxide ion.
The rate determining step is the dissociation of tert-butylbromide.
The reaction rate is proportional to the concentration of tert-butylbromide.
24044.sol:
The given reaction is the nucleophilic substitution of a tertiary alkyl halide (tert-butyl bromide) to form a tertiary alcohol (tert-butyl alcohol).

Tertiary alkyl halides undergo substitution via the $S_N1$ mechanism due to steric hindrance which prevents the $S_N2$ mechanism, and the formation of a stable tertiary carbocation intermediate.

The $S_N1$ mechanism proceeds in two steps:
Step 1: Dissociation of tert-butyl bromide to form a tert-butyl carbocation and a bromide ion. This is the slow, rate-determining step.
Step 2: Attack of the nucleophile ($OH^-$) on the carbocation to form the product.

From this mechanism, we can evaluate the given statements:
1. The rate law for this $S_N1$ reaction is Rate = $k[(CH_3)_3C-Br]$. The rate is proportional to the concentration of tert-butyl bromide, making statement (d) correct.
2. The rate-determining step is the dissociation of tert-butyl bromide, making statement (c) correct.
3. The concentration of the nucleophile ($OH^-$) does not appear in the rate law, so the reaction rate does not change upon increasing its concentration. Statement (b) is correct.
4. $S_N1$ reactions are favored by polar protic solvents because they stabilize the carbocation intermediate and the transition state leading to it through solvation. Water is a more polar solvent than ethyl alcohol. Therefore, changing the solvent from pure ethyl alcohol to a 1:1 mixture of ethyl alcohol and water increases the polarity of the solvent system. This increased polarity will stabilize the intermediate ions better, thereby increasing the reaction rate. Statement (a) claims the rate decreases, which is incorrect.

Answer: The reaction rate decreases upon changing the solvent from ethyl alcohol to 1:1 mixture of ethyl alcohol and water.

28835.text: Number of complexes which will exhibit synergic bonding amongst, $\left[Cr{\left(CO\right)$}_{6}\right], $\left[Mn{\left(CO\right)}_{5}\right]$ and $\left[{Mn}_{2}{\left(CO\right)$}_{10}\right]$ is$
28835.sol:
Synergic bonding involves transference of electrons from ligands to metal. The transference of electrons takes place from filled metal orbitals to anti-bonding orbitals of ligands. It is a bond between a carbonyl group acting as a ligand and a metal. Synergic bonding means self strengthening bond. More the number of d electrons on the central metal ion more the synergic bonding. In metal carbonyls' oxidation state of the metal is zero.

In the complex $\left[Mn{\left(CO\right)$}_{5}\right]$, the electronic configuration of $Mn$ is $3{d}^{5}4{s}^{2}$. As carbon monoxide is a strong field, pairing of electrons occurs. Hence, the new electronic configuration of $Mn$ is $3{d}^{7}.

In the $case of \left[{Mn}_{2}{\left(CO\right)$}_{10}\right]$ also electronic configuration after pairing of electrons is $3{d}^{7}.

In the $complex \left[Cr{\left(CO\right)$}_{6}\right]$ , the electronic configuration of $Cr$ is $3{d}^{5}4{s}^{1}$ . As carbon monoxide is a strong field, pairing of electrons occurs. Hence, the new electronic configuration of $Cr$ is $3{d}^{6}$

All of these compounds can show synergic bonding.

$

30081.sol:
Mond's process involves the combination of carbon monoxide with nickel readily and reversibly and gives nickel tetracarbonyl. This process is used to extract and purify nickel.

The Van Arkel technique is used to refine Zirconium or Titanium. Impurities found in Zirconium or Titanium in the form of nitrogen and oxygen are eliminated using this technique.

Copper is purified by electrolysis. Electricity is passed through solutions containing copper compounds, such as copper sulphate. The anode (positive electrode ) is made from impure copper and the cathode (negative electrode) is made from pure copper.

Mercury and zinc are purified by distillation method. Liquation is a metallurgical method to remove lead containing silver from copper and remove antimony minerals from ore.

31410.text: First and second ionization enthalpies of lithium are $520$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ and $7297$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively. Energy required to convert $3.5$ mg lithium (g) into $\text{Li}^{2+}$(g) $[\text{Li(g)} \rightarrow \text{Li}^{2+}\text{(g)}]$ is _______ kJ mol$^{-1}$. (nearest integer) [Molar mass of Li $= 7$ g mol$^{-1}$]
31410.sol:
The total energy required to convert $1$ mole of $\text{Li(g)}$ to $\text{Li}^{2+}\text{(g)}$ is the sum of the first and second ionization enthalpies:

$E = IE_1 + IE_2 = 520 + 7297 = 7817 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Given mass of lithium $= 3.5 \text{ mg} = 3.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ g}$

Number of moles of lithium $= \dfrac{3.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ g}}{7 \text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}$

Energy required for $5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}$ of Li is:

$\text{Energy} = 5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol} \times 7817 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1} = 3.9085 \text{ kJ}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we get $4$ KJ.

Answer: $4$

32848.text: If $f\left(x\right) = {x}^{2} + {g}^{'}\left(1\right)x + {g}^{"}\left(2\right)$ and $g\left(x\right) = f\left(1\right){x}^{2} + x{f}^{'}\left(x\right) + {f}^{"}\left(x\right)$, then the value of $f\left(4\right) - g\left(4\right)$ is equal to _____ .
32848.sol:
Given:

$f\left(x\right)$ = {x}^{2} + {g}^{'}$\left(1\right)$x + {g}^{"}$\left(2\right)$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 2x + {g}^{'}\left(1\right)

$⇒ {f}^{"}$\left(x\right)$ = 2$

Now,

$g$\left(x\right)$ = f $\left(1\right)${x}^{2} + x{f}^{'}$\left(x\right) + {f}^{"}\left(x\right)

$⇒ g $\left(x\right)$ = f $\left(1\right)${x}^{2} + x $\left[2x + {g}^{'}\left(1\right)$\right] + 2$

$⇒ g $\left(x\right)$ = $\left[f\left(1\right) + 2\right]{x}^{2} + {g}^{'}\left(1\right)x + 2$

$⇒ {g}^{'}\left(x\right) = 2f\left(1\right)x + 4x + {g}^{'}\left(1\right) . . . . \left(1\right)

$⇒ {g}^{"}$\left(x\right)$ = 2f $\left(1\right)$ + 4 . . . $\left(2\right)$

Put x = 1 in $\left(1\right)$, then we get

$2f\left(1\right) + 4 = 0$

$⇒ f\left(1\right) = - 2$

$∴ {g}^{"}\left(2\right) = 2f\left(1\right) + 4 = 0$

Now,

$f\left(x\right) = {x}^{2} + {g}^{'}\left(1\right)x + {g}^{"}\left(2\right)$

Put $x = 1$, then we get

$f\left(1\right)$ = 1 + {g}^{'}$\left(1\right)$ + {g}^{"}$\left(2\right)$

$⇒ {g}^{'}\left(1\right) = - 3$

So,

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 2x - 3$

$f\left(x\right)$ = {x}^{2} - 3x + c$

Since, $f$\left(1\right)$ = - 2 ⇒ c = 0$

So,

$f$\left(x\right) = {x}^{2} - 3x$

And,

$g\left(x\right) = f\left(1\right){x}^{2} + x{f}^{'}\left(x\right)$ + {f}^{"}$\left(x\right)$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = - 2{x}^{2} + x\left(2x - 3\right) + 2$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = - 3x + 2$

Hence, $f\left(4\right) - g\left(4\right) = 4 + 10 = 14$

33424.text: The lowest integer which is greater than ${\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{{10}^{100}}\right)}^{{10}^{100}}$ is
33424.sol:
Consider $P = {\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{{10}^{100}}\right)}^{{10}^{100}},$

Let $x = {10}^{100}$

$⇒ P = {\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)}^{x}$

$⇒ P = 1 + \left(x\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) + \dfrac{\left(x\right)\left(x - 1\right)}{⌊ 2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}} + \dfrac{\left(x\right)\left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right)}{\dfrac{3}{3}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}} + \ldots$

(upto ${10}^{100} + 1$ terms)

$⇒ P = 1 + 1 + \left(\dfrac{1}{⌊ 2} - \dfrac{1}{\left⌊2x\right}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{⌊ 3} - \ldots\right) + \ldots$ so on

$⇒ P = 2 +$(Positive value less than $\dfrac{1}{⌊ 2} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 3} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 4} + \ldots$ )

Also $e = 1 + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 1} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 2} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 3} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 4} + \ldots$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{⌊ 2} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 3} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 4} + \ldots = e - 2$

$⇒ P = 2 +$ (Positive value less than $e - 2$)

$⇒ P \in \left(2, 3\right)$

$⇒$ Least integer value of $P$ is $3 .$

34797.text: If the curve $y = y ( x )$ is the solution of the differential equation $2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)dy - y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)dx = 2{x}^{9 / 4}dx, x > 0$ which passes through the point $\left(1, 1 - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}2\right),$ then the value of $y ( 16 )$ is equal to <gwmw style="display:none;"></gwmw>
34797.sol:
Given differential equation is $2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)dy - y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)dx = 2{x}^{9 / 4}dx$

$⇒ 2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right) = 2{x}^{9 / 4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)}{2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)} = \dfrac{2{x}^{9 / 4}}{2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)}{2x\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)} = \dfrac{2{x}^{9 / 4}}{2{x}^{5 / 4}\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y}{2x} = \dfrac{x}{\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}$

This is a linear differential equation of the type $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$ where $P = - \dfrac{1}{2x}$ and $Q = \dfrac{x}{{x}^{3 / 4} + 1}$

Now, we have integrating factor $I . F . = {e}^{∫ Pdx}$

$= {e}^{- ∫ \dfrac{dx}{2x}} = {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}{\log}_{e}x}$

$= {e}^{{\log}_{e}{x}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}} = {x}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

Now, the solution of the linear differential equation is $y \times \left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q \times \left(I . F .\right)dx + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = ∫ \dfrac{x \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2}}{\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}dx + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = ∫ \dfrac{{x}^{1 / 2}}{\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}dx + C$

Put $x = {t}^{4} ⇒ dx = 4{t}^{3}dt$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = ∫ \dfrac{{t}^{2} \cdot 4{t}^{3}dt}{\left({t}^{3} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = 4 ∫ \dfrac{{t}^{2}\left({t}^{3} + 1 - 1\right)}{\left({t}^{3} + 1\right)}dt$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = 4 ∫ {t}^{2}dt - 4 ∫ \dfrac{{t}^{2}}{{t}^{3} + 1}dt + C$

Let, ${t}^{3} + 1 = u ⇒ 3{t}^{2}dt = du$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = 4 ∫ {t}^{2}dt - \dfrac{4}{3} ∫ \dfrac{du}{u} + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4{t}^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}\left|u\right| + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4{t}^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}\left({t}^{3} + 1\right) + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4{x}^{3 / 4}}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right) + C$

Now, the curve passes through $\left(1, 1 - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}2\right)$

$⇒ 1 - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}2 = \dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}2 + C$

$⇒ C = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4}{3}{x}^{3 / 4} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right) - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{4}{3}{x}^{5 / 4} - \dfrac{4}{3}\sqrt{x}{\log}_{e}\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right) - \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{3}$

Hence, at $x = 16,$ we get

$y ( 16 ) = \dfrac{4}{3} \times 32 - \dfrac{4}{3} \times 4 \times {\log}_{e}9 - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ y\left(16\right) = \dfrac{124}{3} - \dfrac{32}{3}{\log}_{e}3$

$⇒ y\left(16\right) = 4\left(\dfrac{31}{3} - \dfrac{8}{3}{\log}_{e}3\right) .

$

34803.text: The rate of growth of bacteria in a culture is proportional to the number of bacteria present and the bacteria count is $1000$ at initial time $t = 0 .$ The number of bacteria is increased by $20 %$ in $2$ hours. $⇒ ln\dfrac{{B}_{2}}{{B}_{1}} = \lambda\left({t}_{2} - {t}_{1}\right) . . . \left(i\right)$

Given that, at $t = 0, B = 1000 \text{ and } t = 20 % \text{increase} = 1200$

$∴ ln\dfrac{1200}{1000} = 2\lambda ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}ln\dfrac{6}{5}$

Now an equation $\left(i\right)$becomes,

$ln\dfrac{{B}_{2}}{{B}_{1}} = \dfrac{1}{2}ln\dfrac{6}{5}\left({t}_{2} - {t}_{1}\right) . . . \left(ii\right)$

Given that, at ${t}_{2} = \dfrac{k}{ln2}, {B}_{2} = 2000 \text{ and } t = 0, {B}_{1} = 1000$

From $\left(ii\right), ln\dfrac{2000}{1000} = \dfrac{1}{2}ln\dfrac{6}{5}\left(\dfrac{k}{ln\dfrac{6}{5}} - 0\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}k$

$⇒ k = 2ln2$

$∴ {\left(\dfrac{k}{ln2}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{2ln2}{ln2}\right)}^{2} = 4$

35009.text: The line $x = 8$ is the directrix of the ellipse $E: \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$ with the corresponding focus $\left(2, 0\right)$. If the tangent to $E$ at the point $P$ in the first quadrant passes through the point $\left(0, 4\sqrt{3}\right)$ and intersects the $x$-axis at $Q$, then ${\left(3PQ\right)}^{2}$ is equal to _____ .

Given,

The line $x = 8$ is the directrix of the ellipse $E: \dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$ with the corresponding focus $\left(2, 0\right)$,

So, equation of directrix is given by $x = \dfrac{a}{e} ⇒ 8 = \dfrac{a}{e} \ldots \left(1\right)$

And distance of corresponding focus is given by,

$ae = 2 \ldots \left(2\right)$

So, from both equation we get,

$8e = \dfrac{2}{e}$

$⇒ e^{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}⇒ e = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Hence, $a = 4$

Now using eccentricity formula we get,

$b^{2} = a^{2}\left(1 - e^{2}\right)= 16\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) =12$

Now equation of tangent to ellipse at point $P \l$left(4cos\theta, \s$ sqrt{12}sin\theta\right)$ is given by,

$\dfrac{xcos\theta}{4} +\dfrac{ysin\theta}{2\sqrt{3}} =1$

Now given tangent passes through $\left(0, 4\sqrt{3}\right),

So, sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$⇒ $\theta =30 °$

Now, point $P \$lleft(4cos\theta, \s$ ssqrt{12}sin\theta\right)$ will be& $P \l left(2\sqrt{3}, \sqrt{3}\right)$

And intersection of tangent with $x -$axis will give $Q $\$left(\dfrac{8}{3},0\right)$

Hence, by distance formula we get, $\left(3PQ\right)2 = 39$

37726.text: In a triangle $ABC$, if $cosA + 2cosB + cosC = 2$ and the lengths of the sides opposite to the angles $A$ and $C$ are $3$ and $7$ respectively, then $cosA - cosC$ is equal to
37726.sol:
Given,

$AB = 7, BC = 3$.

$⇒ c = 7, a = 3$.

Apply cosine rule in the given equation $cosA + 2cosB + cosC = 2$, we get

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{{b}^{2} + {c}^{2} - {a}^{2}}{2bc}\right) + 2\left(\dfrac{{c}^{2} + {a}^{2} - {b}^{2}}{2ac}\right) + \left(\dfrac{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} - {c}^{2}}{2ab}\right) = 2$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{{b}^{2} + 49 - 9}{14b}\right) + \left(\dfrac{49 + 9 - {b}^{2}}{21}\right) + \left(\dfrac{9 + {b}^{2} - 49}{6b}\right) = 2$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{{b}^{2} + 40}{14b}\right) + \left(\dfrac{58 - {b}^{2}}{21}\right) + \left(\dfrac{{b}^{2} - 40}{6b}\right) = 2$

$⇒ {b}^{3} - 5{b}^{2} - 16b + 80 = 0$

$⇒ \left(b - 4\right)\left(b + 4\right)\left(b - 5\right) = 0$

$⇒ b = - 4, 4, 5$.

But $b \ne - 4$.

Also, if $b = 4$ triangle cannot be constructed.

That means $b = 5$.

$⇒ cosA - cosC = \left(\dfrac{{b}^{2} + {c}^{2} - {a}^{2}}{2bc}\right) - \left(\dfrac{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} - {c}^{2}}{2ab}\right)$

$⇒ cosA - cosC = \left(\dfrac{{5}^{2} + {7}^{2} - {3}^{2}}{2\left(5 \times 7\right)}\right) - \left(\dfrac{{3}^{2} + {5}^{2} - {7}^{2}}{2\left(3 \times 5\right)}\right)$

$⇒ cosA - cosC = \left(\dfrac{65}{70}\right) - \left(\dfrac{- 15}{30}\right) = \dfrac{195 + 105}{210} = \dfrac{300}{210}$

$⇒ cosA - cosC = \dfrac{10}{7}$

$⇒ a = 4$

47732.subject: Chemistry
47732.text: Which of the following will not act as an oxidising agent?
47732.sol:
In Group 6 elements (Cr, Mo, W), the stability of the higher oxidation state (+6) increases down the group.

Therefore, Mo(VI) and W(VI) are much more stable than Cr(VI).

Compounds of Cr(VI) such as $\text{CrO}_3$, $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$, and $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ are strong oxidising agents because Cr(VI) can easily be reduced to the more stable Cr(III) state.

On the other hand, Mo(VI) in $\text{MoO}_3$ is highly stable and does not undergo reduction easily. Thus, $\text{MoO}_3$ does not act as an oxidising agent.

Answer: $\text{MoO}_3$

47773.subject: Chemistry
47773.text: In a transition series, with increase in atomic-number, the paramagnetism
options: first increases to a maximum and then decreases
first decreases to a minimum and then increases
47773.sol:
The paramagnetism of transition elements of a given series increases on moving left to right in a period and attain a maximum value and after that, it goes on decreasing towards the end of period. This is due to the fact that the magnetic moment or paramagnetism is directly related to the number of half-filled $d$-orbitals. In the beginning, the number of unpaired electrons in $d$-orbitals increases till the middle of the period $\left(d^{1}\right.$ to $\left.d^{5}\right)$. After this, the pairing of electrons occurs in $d$-orbitals $\left(d^{6}\right.$ to $\left.d^{10}\right)$.
Thus, in a given transition series, with increases in atomic-number, the paramagnetism first increases to a maximum and then decreases.

When electron jumps from \( n=4 \) level to \( n=1 \) level, the angular momentum of electron
changes by
49787.sol:
Given, electron jumps from \( n=4 \) level to \( n=1 \) level. Angular momentum \( L \) is given as \( L=n $\frac{h}{2 I I}$\)
Therefore, \( $L_{n=4}=\frac{4 h}{2 \Pi}$\) and \( $L_{n=1}=\frac{h}{2 \Pi}$\)
Change in angular momentum \(\Delta $L=L_{n=4}-L_{n=1}=\frac{4 h}{2 \pi}-\frac{h}{2 \Pi}$\)
Thus \(\Delta $L=\frac{3 h}{2 \Pi}$\)

53883.text: If the integers $m$ and $n$ are chosen at random between 1 and 100 , then the probability that a number of the form $7^m+7^n$ is divisible by 5 , equals
53883.sol:
Since, $m$ and $n$ are selected between 1 and 100 , hence sample space $=100 \times 100$ Also, $\quad 7^1=1,7^2=49,7^3=343,7^4=24017^5=16807$ etc.
Hence, 1, 3, 7 and 9 will be the last digits in the power of 7. Hence, for favourable cases. $\begin{array}{lllllll}{c}{nm}\\ \text{ and } \text{ and } \downarrow \text{ and } \text{ and } \\1,2 \text{ and } 1,2 \text{ and } 1,3 \text{ and } \ldots \text{ and } 1,100 \text{ and } \\2,1 \text{ and } 2,2 \text{ and } 2,3 \text{ and } \ldots \text{ and } 2,100 \\100,1 \text{ and } 100,2 \text{ and } 100,3 \text{ and } \ldots \text{ and } 100,100\end{array}
\therefore$ favourable cases $=25$ for $m=2, \quad n=4,8,12,10 \quad \ldots \quad 100\therefore$ favourable cases $=25$ Similarly for every $m$, favourable $n$ are 25. $\therefore$ Total favourable cases $=100 \times 25$ Hence, required probability $=\frac{100 \times 25}{100 \times 100}=\frac{1}{4}$

53944.sol:
We have, $a^2, b^2$ and $c^2$ are in AP adding $a b+b c+c a$ to each of these terms, we get $a^2+a b+b c+c a, b^2+a b+b c+c a$ and $c^2+a b+b c+c a$ are in AP.
$\Rightarrow(a+b)(a+c),(b+c)(b+a) \text{ and }(c+a)(c+b)$ are in AP.
Dividing each term by $(b+c)(c+a)(a+b)$, we get
$\frac{1}{b+c}, \frac{1}{c+a}$ and $\frac{1}{a+b}$ are in AP
$\Rightarrow b+c, c+a$ and $a+b$ are in HP.

Subtracting Eq. (ii) from Eq. (i),

So, $1+\mu=0 and 1+\lambda=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=\mu=-1$
Therefore, \mathbf{a}+\mathrm{b}=$- $\mathbf{c} \begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{c}=0 \Rightarrow|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{c}|^2=0 \\
& \Rightarrow|\mathbf{a}|^2+|\mathbf{b}|^2+|\mathbf{c}|^2+2(\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}+\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{c}+\mathbf{c} \cdot \mathbf{a})=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 2+2+2+2(\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}+\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{c}+\mathbf{c} \cdot \mathbf{a})=0 \\

54584.text: A sinusoidal wave travelling in the positive direction on stretched string has amplitude 20 cm , wavelength 1 m and wave velocity $5 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$. At $x=0$ and $t=0$, it is given that $y=0$ and $\frac{d y}{d t} < 0$. Find the wave function $y(x, t)$.
options: $y(x, t)=(0.02 m) \sin \left[\left(2 \pi \mathrm{ m}^{-1}\right) x+\left(10 \pi \mathrm{ s}^{-1}\right) t\right] \mathrm{m}$
$y(x, t)=(0.02 m) \cos \left[\left(10 \pi \mathrm{ s}^{-1}\right) t+\left(2 \pi \mathrm{ m}^{-1}\right) x\right] \mathrm{m}$
$y(x, t)=(0.02 m) \sin \left[\left(2 \pi \mathrm{ m}^{-1}\right) x-\left(10 \pi \mathrm{ s}^{-1}\right) t\right] \mathrm{m}$
54584.sol:
We start a general form for a rightward moving wave,
$y(x, t)=A \sin (k x-\omega t+\phi)$...(i)
The given amplitude is $A=2 \mathrm{ cm}=0.02 \mathrm{ m}$
The wavelength is given as
$\lambda=1 \mathrm{ m}$
Wave number $=k=2 \pi / \lambda=2 \pi \mathrm{ m}^{-1}$
Angular frequency,
$\omega=v k=10 \pi \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
From Eq. (i),
$\because \quad \begin{aligned} y(x, t) & =(0.02) \sin [2 \pi(x-5 t)+\phi] \\ \text{ For } x & =0, t=0 \\ y & =0 \text{ and } \frac{\partial y}{\partial t} < 0\end{aligned}$
i.e. $\quad 0.02 \sin \phi=0$
(as $y=0$ )
and $\quad-0.2 \pi \cos \phi < 0$
From these conditions, we may conclude that $\phi=2 n \pi$, where $n=0,2,4,6, \ldots$
Therefore,
$y(x, t)=(0.02 \mathrm{ m}) \sin \left[\left(2 \pi \mathrm{ m}^{-1}\right) \mathrm{x}-\left(10 \pi \mathrm{ s}^{-1}\right) t\right] \mathrm{m}$

54718.subject: Physics
54718.text: When a copper sphere is heated, percentage change is
options: equal in radius, volume and density
54718.sol:
Let $R$ be the radius of sphere, $V$ its volume and $\rho$ its density. Then,
$\Delta R=R \alpha \Delta \theta$
and percentage change in radius
$\frac{\Delta R}{R} \times 100=100 \alpha \Delta \theta$ ...(i)
Now, $\quad \Delta V=\gamma v \Delta \theta=3 \alpha v \Delta \theta \quad\{\because \gamma=3 \alpha\}\therefore$ Percentage increase in volume
$=\frac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100=300 \alpha \Delta \theta$ ...(ii)
Again, $\quad \rho^{\prime}=\frac{\rho}{1+\gamma \Delta \theta}=\frac{\rho}{1+3 \alpha \Delta \theta}\therefore \quad \Delta \rho=\rho-\rho^{\prime}=\rho\left[1-\frac{1}{1+3 \alpha \Delta \theta}\right]=\frac{(3 \alpha \Delta \theta) \rho}{1+3 \alpha \Delta \theta}$
Percentage change in density
$=\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100=\frac{300 \alpha \Delta \theta}{1+3 \alpha \Delta \theta}$ ...(iii)
From Eqs. (i), (ii) and (iii), we see that the percentage change is maximum in volume.

The cell representation is $\text{Cu}_{(s)} \mid \text{Cu}^{2+}_{(1M)} \| \text{Ag}^{+}_{(1M)} \mid \text{Ag}$.

Since the concentrations of the ions are $1\ \text{M}$, the given emf is the standard emf of the cell, $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = 0.463\ \text{V}$.

The standard reduction potential of the anode (Cu) is $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}} = 0.337\ \text{V}$.

Using the relation for standard cell potential:

$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{anode}}$

$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{Ag}^{+}/\text{Ag}} - E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}}$

Substituting the given values:

$0.463 = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{Ag}^{+}/\text{Ag}} - 0.337$

$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{Ag}^{+}/\text{Ag}} = 0.463 + 0.337 = 0.800\ \text{V}$

The standard potential of the Ag electrode is $0.8\ \text{V}$.

Answer: $0.8\ \text{V}$

57584.text: Which of the following compounds is obtained when Bromoethane is reacted with silver acetate?
57584.sol:
The reaction between bromoethane and silver acetate is a nucleophilic substitution reaction.

The acetate ion ($CH_3COO^-$) acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbon of bromoethane ($CH_3CH_2Br$), displacing the bromide ion.

The chemical equation for the reaction is:
$CH_3CH_2Br + CH_3COOAg \rightarrow CH_3COOCH_2CH_3 + AgBr \downarrow$

The product formed is $CH_3COOCH_2CH_3$, which is ethyl acetate.

Answer: ethyl acetate

The contact process is used for the industrial production of sulfuric acid.

58231.subject: Chemistry
58231.text: Which from following compounds is NOT acidic in nature?
58231.sol:
Oxides are classified as acidic, basic, amphoteric, or neutral. Non-metal oxides are typically acidic, though exceptions exist.

SO_{2} is an oxide of sulfur. It reacts with water to form sulfurous acid: $\mathrm{SO}_2(g) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_3(aq)$, so it is acidic.

CO_{2} is an oxide of carbon. It reacts with water to form carbonic acid: $\mathrm{CO}_2(g) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{CO}_3(aq)$, so it is acidic.

N_{2}O_{5} is an oxide of nitrogen. It reacts with water to form nitric acid: $\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_5(s) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{HNO}_3(aq)$, so it is acidic.

N_{2}O is also an oxide of nitrogen, but it is a neutral oxide and does not react with acids or bases, like CO and NO. Therefore, it is not acidic.

The oxide that is not acidic is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

59559.text: If compressibility factor of real gas is 1.05 at STP. What is molar volume of real gas?
59559.sol:
The compressibility factor $Z$ for a real gas is defined as $Z = \frac{V_{m,\text{real}}}{V_{m,\text{ideal}}}$.

At STP, the molar volume of an ideal gas is known to be $22.4\ \text{dm}^3$.

Given $Z = 1.05$, the molar volume of the real gas becomes $V_{m,\text{real}} = Z \times V_{m,\text{ideal}} = 1.05 \times 22.4 = 23.52\ \text{dm}^3$.

Among the options provided, both C and D state $23.52\ \text{dm}^3$, representing the correct value.

59896.subject: Chemistry
59896.text: A gas expands from a volume of $1$ dm^3$ to $1.25$ dm^3$ under a pressure of $1$ bar. Find the change in internal energy if $150$ J of heat is supplied to the system.
59896.sol:
Given $V_1 = 1$ dm^3$ and $V_2 = 1.25$ dm^3$.

Change in volume, $\Delta V = 1.25 - 1 = 0.25$ dm^3 = 0.25$ L.

External pressure, $P = 1$ bar.

Work done during expansion is given by $W = -P \Delta V$.

$W = -1 \times 0.25 = -0.25$ L bar.

Since $1$ L bar $= 100$ J, we have $W = -0.25 \times 100 = -25$ J.

Heat supplied to the system, $q = 150$ J.

According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + W$.

$\Delta U = 150 - 25 = 125$ J.

Answer: $125 J

60705.subject: Mathematics
60705.text: The equation of a circle whose center lies on $x + 2y = 0$ and touching the lines $3x - 4y + 8 = 0$ and $3x - 4y - 28 = 0$ is
60705.sol:
The given lines $3x - 4y + 8 = 0$ and $3x - 4y - 28 = 0$ are parallel. The distance between them is the diameter of the circle.

Diameter $= \dfrac{|8 - (-28)|}{\sqrt{3^2 + (-4)^2}} = \dfrac{36}{5}$

Radius $r = \dfrac{18}{5}$

The center of the circle lies on the line parallel to and midway between the two given lines. The equation of this midway line is:

$3x - 4y + \dfrac{8 + (-28)}{2} = 0 \Rightarrow 3x - 4y - 10 = 0$

The center also lies on the given line $x + 2y = 0$.

Solving $3x - 4y - 10 = 0$ and $x + 2y = 0$, we substitute $x = -2y$:

$3(-2y) - 4y - 10 = 0 \Rightarrow -10y = 10 \Rightarrow y = -1$

Substituting $y = -1$ in $x = -2y$, we get $x = 2$.

The center of the circle is $(2,-1)$.

The equation of the circle is:

$(x - 2)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = \left(\dfrac{18}{5}\right)^2$

$(x - 2)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = \dfrac{324}{25}$

$25(x - 2)^2 + 25(y + 1)^2 = 324$

Answer: $25(x - 2)^2 + 25(y + 1)^2 = 324$

61644.subject: Mathematics
61644.text: Let $y = \sqrt[p]{x^3 y}$. If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3}{2}$ when $y = 1$, then the value of $p$ is equal to $\ldots$
61644.sol:
Given $y = \sqrt[p]{x^3 y}$

Raising both sides to the power $p$:

$y^p = x^3 y$

$y^{p-1} = x^3$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$(p-1) y^{p-2} \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2$

When $y = 1$, from $y^{p-1} = x^3$, we get $x^3 = 1 \Rightarrow x = 1$.

Substituting $x = 1$, $y = 1$, and $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3}{2}$ into the differentiated equation:

$(p-1) (1)^{p-2} \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = 3(1)^2$

$(p-1) \dfrac{3}{2} = 3$

$p - 1 = 2$

$p = 3$

Answer: $3$

62503.sol:
Let $I=\int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{x d x}{(1+x)\left(x^{2}+1\right)}$
By partial fraction, $\frac{x}{(1+x)\left(x^{2}+1\right)}=\frac{A}{(1+x)}+\frac{B x+C}{\left(x^{2}+1\right)}\Rightarrow x=A\left(x^{2}+1\right)+(1+x)(B x+C)\Rightarrow x=A\left(x^{2}+1\right)+\left(B x+B x^{2}+C+C x\right)\Rightarrow x=(A+B) x^{2}+(B+C) x+(A+C)$
On comparing both sides, we get A+B=0, \quad B+C=1, \quad A+C=0 \quad \ldots($\mathrm{i}$)$On adding all these equations, we get \begin{aligned} A+B+C &=\frac{1}{2}...(ii) \\ \therefore \quad A=\frac{1}{2}-1 &=-\frac{1}{2}, \quad C=\frac{1}{2} \\ \text{$ and $} \quad B=\frac{1}{2} \\ \therefore \quad I=\int_{0}^{\infty}\left\{\frac{-1}{2(1+x)}+\frac{1}{2} \frac{(x+1)}{\left(x^{2}+1\right)}\right\} d x \\=-\frac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{d x}{1+x}+\frac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{x}{x^{2}+1} d x \\+\frac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{d x}{1+x^{2}} \end{aligned}=-\frac{1}{2}[\log (1+x)]_{0}^{\infty}+\frac{1}{4}\left[\log \left(x^{2}+1\right)\right]_{0}^{\infty}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{\pi}{2}=-\frac{1}{2} \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \log (1+x)+\frac{1}{4}\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \log \left(1+x^{2}\right)+\frac{\pi}{4}=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \log \left[\frac{\left(1+x^{2}\right)^{1 / 4}}{(1+x)^{1 / 2}}\right]+\frac{\pi}{4}=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \log \left[\frac{\sqrt{x}\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}+1\right)^{1 / 4}}{\sqrt{x}\left(\frac{1}{x}+1\right)^{1 / 2}}\right]+\frac{\pi}{4}=\log \frac{(0+1)^{1 / 4}}{(0+1)^{1 / 2}}+\frac{\pi}{4}=\log (1)+\frac{\pi}{4}=0+\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{4}$

62837.subject: Mathematics
62837.text: If the difference between the maximum and minimum values of the objective function $\mathrm{z}=7 x-8 \mathrm{y}$ subject to the constraints $x+y \leqslant 20$, $y \geqslant 5, x, y \geqslant 0$ is $5 k+200$, then the value of $k$ is
62837.sol:
Identifying feasible region vertices

The feasible region is bounded by the constraints: $x + y \leq 20$, $y \geq 5$, and $x \geq 0$.
Intersection of $x = 0$ and $y = 5$ gives vertex $(0,5)$.
Intersection of $y = 5$ and $x + y = 20$ gives vertex $(15,5)$.
Intersection of $x = 0$ and $x + y = 20$ gives vertex $(0,20)$.

Evaluating objective function

$z = 7x - 8y$ at $(0,5)$ yields $z = -40$, at $(15,5)$ yields $z = 65$, and at $(0,20)$ yields $z = -160$.
The maximum is $65$ and the minimum is $-160$.

Solving for k

$\text{Maximum} - \text{Minimum} = 65 - (-160) = 225$

$225 = 5k + 200$

$5k = 25$

64195.text: The area of a triangle formed by a line with the coordinate axes is $49$ sq. units. If the perpendicular drawn from the origin to this line makes an angle of $45^{}^{\circ}$ with the positive X-axis, then the equation of line is....
64195.sol:
Let the equation of the line in normal form be $x \cos \alpha + y \sin \alpha = p$.

Given $\alpha = 45^{}^{\circ}$, the equation becomes $x \cos 45^{}^{\circ} + y \sin 45^{}^{\circ} = p$, which simplifies to $x + y = p\sqrt{2}$.

The x-intercept is $a = p\sqrt{2}$ and the y-intercept is $b = p\sqrt{2}$.

The area of the triangle formed with the coordinate axes is $\dfrac{1}{2}ab = 49$.

Substituting the intercepts, we get $\dfrac{1}{2}(p\sqrt{2})(p\sqrt{2}) = 49$.

This gives $p^2 = 49$, so $p = 7$ (since perpendicular distance $p > 0$).

Therefore, the equation of the line is $x + y = 7\sqrt{2}$.

Answer: $x + y = 7\sqrt{2}$

66823.text: The self-inductance of a circuit is numerically equal to

69208.text: Two discs $A$ and $B$ of same material and thickness have radii $R$ and $3 R$ respectively. Their moments of inertia about their axis will be in the ratio
69208.sol:
Key concept: The moment of inertia of a homogeneous disc about its central axis is $I = \frac{1}{2} M R^2$, where mass scales proportionally to the square of the radius for constant thickness and density.

Given $R_B = 3R_A$, it follows from $M \propto R^2$ that $M_B = 9M_A$.

Then for disc A: $I_A = \frac{1}{2} M_A R_A^2$
For disc B: $I_B = \frac{1}{2} (9M_A) (3R_A)^2 = \frac{1}{2} (9M_A)(9R_A^2) = \frac{81}{2} M_A R_A^2$

The ratio is $\frac{I_A}{I_B} = \frac{ \frac{1}{2} M_A R_A^2 }{ \frac{81}{2} M_A R_A^2 } = \frac{1}{81}$

Final answer: $\boxed{C}$

69211.subject: Physics
69211.text: A body slides down a smooth inclined plane of inclination $\theta$ and reaches the bottom with velocity V. If the same body is a ring which rolls down the same inclined plane then linear velocity at the bottom of plane is
69211.sol:
The body of mass $m$ descends from height $h$ on an inclined plane.

For sliding without friction: Mechanical energy conservation gives $mgh = \frac{1}{2}mV^2$, so $V^2 = 2gh$.

For a ring rolling without slipping: The moment of inertia is $I = mR^2$, and the velocity relation is $\omega = V_\text{ring}/R$. Energy conservation yields $mgh = \frac{1}{2}mV_\text{ring}^2 + \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2 = \frac{1}{2}mV_\text{ring}^2 + \frac{1}{2}mR^2(V_\text{ring}/R)^2 = mV_\text{ring}^2$. Thus, $V_\text{ring}^2 = gh$.

Substituting $gh = V^2/2$ from the sliding case, $V_\text{ring}^2 = V^2/2$, so $V_\text{ring} = V/\sqrt{2}$.

The linear velocity of the ring is $\boxed{\text{A}}$.

70454.text: A musical instrument P produces sound waves of frequency 'n' and amplitude 'A'. Another musical instrument Q produces sound waves of frequency n/4. The waves produced by P and Q have equal energies. The amplitude of waves produced by Q will be
70454.sol:
The energy of a sound wave is directly proportional to the square of its frequency and the square of its amplitude.

$E \propto f^2 A^2$

Given that the waves produced by P and Q have equal energies:

$E_P = E_Q$

$f_P^2 A_P^2 = f_Q^2 A_Q^2$

Substituting the given values $f_P = n$, $A_P = A$, and $f_Q = \dfrac{n}{4}$:

$n^2 A^2 = \left(\dfrac{n}{4}\right)^2 A_Q^2$

$n^2 A^2 = \dfrac{n^2}{16} A_Q^2$

$A_Q^2 = 16 A^2$

$A_Q = 4A$

Answer: $4A$

70509.sol:
Wave velocity is determined using the fundamental relationship $v = f \lambda$, where $f$ is frequency and $\lambda$ is wavelength.

Frequency is computed as waves per second. Given 45 waves in 60 seconds:

$f = \frac{45}{60} = 0.75$ Hz

Substituting $f = 0.75$ Hz and $\lambda = 7$ m:

$v = 0.75 \times 7 = 5.25$ m/s

The calculated velocity of 5.25 m/s corresponds to option B.

70550.text: With what velocity an observer should move relative to a stationary source so that a sound of triple the frequency of source is heard by an observer?

\therefore \quad & 3  n=n\l left(1+\frac{v_0}{v}\right)\\
\therefore \quad & 3=1+\frac{v_0}{v}\\
\therefore \quad & \frac{v_0}{v}=2 \quad \Rightarrow v_0=2 v
\end{array}$

70965.subject: Biology
70965.text: Which enzyme in the midgut of insect is instrumental in the release of core toxic fragments from bacterial spores ingested by it?
70965.sol:
Bacillus thuringiensis produces proteinaceous toxins in an inactive form called protoxins.

When an insect ingests these spores or crystals, the alkaline pH of the insect's midgut solubilizes the crystals.

Subsequently, midgut proteinases (proteases) cleave the inactive protoxin into its active core toxic fragments.

These active toxins bind to the surface of midgut epithelial cells, creating pores that cause cell swelling and lysis, eventually leading to the death of the insect.

Answer: Proteinase

71442.subject: Biology
71442.text: Which of the following coenzyme is NOT directly required in any of the steps of the Kreb's cycle?
71442.sol:
The Krebs cycle involves a series of oxidation-reduction and substrate-level phosphorylation reactions.

NAD^+$ is required as a coenzyme for the enzymes isocitrate dehydrogenase, $\alpha$-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and malate dehydrogenase.

FAD is required as a coenzyme for succinate dehydrogenase.

Coenzyme A (CoA) is required by the $\alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex to form succinyl-CoA.

Coenzyme Q (Ubiquinone) is a mobile electron carrier in the electron transport chain (ETC) located in the inner mitochondrial membrane and is not directly involved in any of the steps of the Krebs cycle.

Answer: Coenzyme Q

71700.subject: Chemistry
71700.text: What is the number of electrons in bonding molecular orbitals and antibonding molecular orbitals respectively in $\text{F}_2$ molecule?
71700.sol:
The total number of electrons in the F_2$ molecule is 9 + 9 = 18$. The molecular orbital electronic configuration of F_2$ is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^{*2} \pi_{2p_y}^{*2}$ The number of electrons in bonding molecular orbitals (N_b$) is the sum of electrons in \sigma_{1s}$, $\sigma_{2s}$, $\sigma_{2p_z}$, \pi_{2p_x}$, and $\pi_{2p_y}$ orbitals: $N_b = 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10$ The number of electrons in antibonding molecular orbitals (N_a$) is the sum of electrons in \sigma_{1s}^{*}$, $\sigma_{2s}^{*}$, $\pi_{2p_x}^{*}$, and $\pi_{2p_y}^{*}$ orbitals: $N_a = 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8$ Thus, the number of electrons in bonding and antibonding molecular orbitals are 10 and 8 respectively. Answer: 10 and 8

76672.text: If $z$ is a complex number such that $\frac{z-1}{z+1}$ is purely imaginary, then what is $|z|$ equal to?
76672.sol:
Let $z=x+i y\frac{z-1}{z+1}=\frac{(x-1)+i y}{(x+1)+i y}=\frac{[(x-1)+i y] \times[(x+1)-i y]}{[(x+1)+i y] \times[(x+1)-i y]}=\frac{\left(x^2-1\right)+y^2+i[y(x+1)-y(x-1)]}{(x+1)^2+y^2}=\frac{\left(x^2+y^2-1\right)}{(x+1)^2+y^2}+i \frac{(2 y)}{(x+1)^2+y^2}\because$ It is purely imaginary,
$\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1}{z+1}\right)=0\frac{x^2+y^2-1}{(x+1)^2+y^2}=0\therefore \quad x^2+y^2-1=0x^2+y^2=1|z|^2=1|z|=1$

77689.subject: Mathematics
77689.text:
Consider the following in respect of non-singular matrices $A$ and $B$:
I. $(AB)^{-1} = A^{-1}B^{-1}$
II. $(BA)(AB)^{-1} = I$, where $I$ is the identity matrix
III. $(AB)^T = A^T B^T$
How many of the above are correct?
77689.sol:
For Statement I, the reversal law of matrix inverse gives $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$. Since matrix multiplication is not commutative in general, $B^{-1}A^{-1} \neq A^{-1}B^{-1}$. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.

For Statement II, using the reversal law, $(BA)(AB)^{-1} = (BA)(B^{-1}A^{-1}) = B(AB^{-1})A^{-1} = BIA^{-1} = BA^{-1}$. This is not equal to $I$ in general. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

For Statement III, the reversal law of matrix transpose gives $(AB)^T = B^T A^T$. Since matrix multiplication is not commutative, $B^T A^T \neq A^T B^T$ in general. Thus, Statement III is incorrect.

Since none of the statements are correct, the number of correct statements is zero.

Answer: None

79152.sol:
From trigonometric values
1. $\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}
2. \tan \left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)=\tan \left(\pi-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-1
3. \tan \left(\frac{5 \pi}{4}\right)=\tan \left(\pi+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=1
4. \tan \left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)=\tan \left(\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=-\sqrt{3}$

79243.subject: Mathematics
79243.text: $ABC$ is a triangle right-angled at $B$. If $A(k, 1, -1)$, $B(2k, 0, 2)$ and $C(2+2k, k, 1)$ are the vertices of the triangle, then what is the value of $k$?
79243.sol:
The direction ratios of the line segment $AB$ are $(k - 2k, 1 - 0, -1 - 2) = (-k, 1, -3)$.

The direction ratios of the line segment $BC$ are $(2+2k - 2k, k - 0, 1 - 2) = (2, k, -1)$.

Since the triangle is right-angled at $B$, the line segments $AB$ and $BC$ are perpendicular to each other.

Therefore, the dot product of their direction ratios is zero.

$(-k)(2) + (1)(k) + (-3)(-1) = 0$

$-2k + k + 3 = 0$

$k = 3$

Answer: $3$

80914.text: In which one of the following species the central atom has the type of hybridisation which is not the same as that present in the other three?
80914.sol:
Key Idea:- Molecules having the same number of hybrid orbitals, have same hybridisation and number of hybrid orbitals,
$\mathrm{H}=\frac{1}{2}[\mathrm{ V}+\mathrm{X}-\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{A}]$
where, $\mathrm{V}=$ no. of valence electrons of central atom
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{X}=\text{ no. of monovalent atoms } \\
& \mathrm{C}=\text{ charge on cation } \\
& \mathrm{A}=\text{ Charge on anion. }
\end{aligned}$
(a) In $\mathrm{SF}_4 \mathrm{H}=\frac{1}{2}[6+4-0+0)=5$
(b) $\operatorname{In I}_3^{-} \mathrm{H}=\frac{1}{2}[7+2+1]=5$
(c) In $\mathrm{SbCl}_5^{2-}$,
$\mathrm{H}=\frac{1}{2}[5+5+2)=6$
(d) In $\mathrm{PCl}_5$,
$H=\frac{1}{2}[5+5+0-0]=5$
Since, only $\mathrm{SbCl}_5^{2-}$ has different number of hybrid orbitals (ie, 6) from the other given species, its hybridisation is different from the others, ie, $s p^3 d^2$. (The hybridisation of other species is $\operatorname{sp}^$3 $\mathrm{ d} ).$

83993.text: Some of the characteristics of $B t$ cotton are
options: long fibre and resistance to aphids
medium yield, long fibre and resistance to beetle pests
high yield and production of toxic protein crystals which kill dipteran pests
high yield and resistance to bollworms
83993.sol: Bacillus thuringiensis forms crystals containing a toxic insecticidal protein. Bt toxin protein exists as inactive protein but once an insect ingests the inactive toxin, it is converted into an active form of toxin due to the alkaline $\mathrm{pH}$ of the gut, which solubulise the crystals. The activated toxin binds to the surface of midgut epithelial cells and creates pores that cause cell swelling and lysis and eventually cause death of the insect. Specific Bt toxin genes were isolated from $B$. thuringiensis and incorporated into the several plants such as cotton. The toxin is coded by a gene named cry. There are a number of them, $\mathrm{eg}$, the proteins encoded by the genes cry IAc and cry II Ab control the cotton bollworms, that of cry IAb control corn borers.

84702.subject: Zoology
84702.text: The number of vertebrae in a human is __________.
84702.sol:
The vertebral column in an adult human consists of $26$ serially arranged units called vertebrae.

The distribution of vertebrae is as follows:
Cervical vertebrae: $7$
Thoracic vertebrae: $12$
Lumbar vertebrae: $5$
Sacral vertebra: $1$ (fused from $5$ bones)
Coccygeal vertebra: $1$ (fused from $4$ bones)

Total number of vertebrae = $7 + 12 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 26$.

Answer: $26$

90880.sol:
Let, the width of the road the road is $d.$

If the angle of the elevation is $\theta,$ then

$tan\theta = \dfrac{20}{d},$ here $20$ is the diﬀerence between the heights of ${T}_{1}$ and ${T}_{2}.$

Given that, the angle of depression is twice of the angle of elevation.

$tan ⁡ 2\theta = \dfrac{60}{d}$

We know, $tan ⁡ 2\theta = \dfrac{2tan ⁡ \theta}{1 - \tan^{2} ⁡ \theta}$

$∴ \dfrac{60}{d} = \dfrac{40 / d}{1 - \left(400 / d^{2}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{400}{d^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$d = 20\sqrt{3}$

95278.subject: Botany
95278.text: Lysigenous cavity in monocot stems vascular bundles developed by the dissolution of _________.
95278.sol: There are four tissue systems present in monocot stems i.e. dermal tissue system, hypodermal tissue system, ground tissue system, and vascular bundle system. There are barrel-shaped parenchymatous cells found in the epidermis. Trichomes are absent in the monocot stem and below the epidermis, there is a layer of the hypodermal cell present. The ground tissue is undifferentiated in monocot stem which is made up of loosely arranged parenchyma cells. There is a vascular bundle which is found scattered in the ground tissue. Xylem is found on the inner side whereas phloem on the outer side and cambium is absent in monocot stem. So, the inner protoxylem is non-functional and remains water-filled. This water-filled cavity is called the lysigenous cavity or protoxylem cavity.&

96241.subject: Botany
96241.text: Meiosis is one of the two cell division process observed to occur in cells. Which statement from below correctly describes the outcome of a successful meiotic division?
options: Four daughter cells are produced. Each resulting daughter cell has the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
Two daughter cells are produced Each resulting daughter cell has the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
Four daughter cells are produced. Each resulting daughter cell has one-half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
Two daughter cells are produced. Each resulting daughter cell has one-half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
96241.sol:
Meiotic division is a type of cell division where two cell division occurs with only one round of DNA duplication process. The eventual new cells that are formed have half the genetic content of the participating cells. If a participating cell has $20$ chromosome, its eventual daughter cell will have 10 chromosome. Thus, the statement of each daughter cell having one-half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell is the correct one.

Mitosis is another type of cell division process where the DNA duplication occurs once and the cell also divides one time. The resulting daughter cells formed have the same amount of genetic content as the parent cell.

97766.subject: Botany
97766.sol:
Respiration is part of the metabolic process where the nutrients are converted into useful energy for regular cell activities. It is in two-mode depending on the presence or absence of oxygen. Aerobic respiration is the one where oxygen is involved and anaerobic respiration is the process where oxygen is absent.

Respiration is generally considered catabolic as the complex compounds are broken into simpler forms to produce energy. Although, respiration has been found to be both catabolic and anabolic. Protein and fatty acids are broken down into acetyl-CoA, which will be used in the aerobic respiratory process. This acetyl-CoA can also be used in the process of manufacturing fatty acids and protein by stopping the respiratory pathway as per the need of the cell. This process is anabolic as compounds are synthesized. Thus, the respiratory process is considered to be amphibolic - anabolic as well as catabolic.

100408.subject: Physics
100408.text: A metro train starts from rest and in 5 s achieves $108 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$. After that it moves with constant velocity and comes to rest after travelling 45 m with uniform retardation. If total distance travelled is 395 m, find total time of travelling.
100408.sol:
Given, $v=108 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}=30 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
For first equation of motion
$v=u+a t \therefore \quad 30=0+a \times 5 \quad(\because u=0)
or \quad a=6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$
So, distance travelled by metro train in 5 s
$s_1=\frac{1}{2} a t^2=\frac{1}{2} \times(6) \times(5)^2=75 \mathrm{~m}$
Distance travelled before coming to rest
$=45 \mathrm{~m}$
So, from third equation of motion
$\begin{aligned} & 0^2=(30)^2-2 a^{\prime} \times 45 \\ & \text{ or } \quad a^{\prime}=\frac{30 \times 30}{2 \times 45}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2 \\ & \end{aligned}$
Time taken in travelling 45 m is
$t_3=\frac{30}{10}=3 \mathrm{~s}$
Now, total distance $=395 \mathrm{~m}$
ie, $\quad 75+s^{\prime}+45=395 \mathrm{~m}$ or $s^{\prime}=395-(75+45)=275 \mathrm{~m}\therefore \quad t_2=\frac{275}{30}=9.2 \mathrm{~s}$
Hence, total time taken in whole journey
$\begin{aligned} & =t_1+t_2+t_3 \\ & =5+9.2+3 \\ & =17.2 \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$

103145.subject: Physics
103145.text: An air-filled parallel plate capacitor is charged by a battery so that it stores an electrostatic energy $U_{0}$. The battery is then disconnected. A dielectric slab of dielectric constant $K = 2$ and thickness equal to half the plate separation ($\dfrac{d}{2}$) is inserted between the plates. The new electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor will be:
103145.sol:
Let the initial capacitance be $C_{0} = \dfrac{\epsilon_{0}A}{d}$.
The initial energy stored is $U_{0} = \dfrac{Q^{2}}{2C_{0}}$, where $Q$ is the charge on the plates.

When the battery is disconnected, the charge $Q$ remains constant.

A dielectric slab of thickness $t = \dfrac{d}{2}$ and $K = 2$ is inserted. The new capacitance $C$ is:
$C = \dfrac{\epsilon_{0}A}{d - t + \dfrac{t}{K}} = \dfrac{\epsilon_{0}A}{d - \dfrac{d}{2} + \dfrac{d}{4}}$

$C = \dfrac{\epsilon_{0}A}{\dfrac{3d}{4}} = \dfrac{4}{3}C_{0}$

The new energy stored in the capacitor is:
$U = \dfrac{Q^{2}}{2C} = \dfrac{Q^{2}}{2 \left(\dfrac{4}{3}C_{0}\right)}$

$U = \dfrac{3}{4} \left(\dfrac{Q^{2}}{2C_{0}}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4}U_{0}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{4}U_{0}$

103303.subject: Physics
103303.text: A uniform resistance wire of length $L$ and total resistance $100\ \Omega$ is connected across an ideal $10\ \text{V}$ battery. A voltmeter with a finite internal resistance of $100\ \Omega$ is used to measure the potential difference across the first half of the wire (length $L/2$). What is the percentage error in the voltmeter reading compared to the true potential difference that would exist without the voltmeter connected?
103303.sol:
Without the voltmeter, the wire acts as two $50\ \Omega$ resistors in series. The true potential difference across the first half is $V_{\text{true}} = 10 \times \dfrac{50}{100} = 5\ \text{V}$.

When the voltmeter is connected, it is in parallel with the first $50\ \Omega$ segment. The equivalent resistance of this parallel combination is $R_p = \dfrac{100 \times 50}{100 + 50} = \dfrac{100}{3}\ \Omega$.

The total resistance of the circuit becomes $R_{\text{total}} = R_p + 50 = \dfrac{100}{3} + 50 = \dfrac{250}{3}\ \Omega$.

The voltage measured by the voltmeter is $V_{\text{measured}} = 10 \times \dfrac{R_p}{R_{\text{total}}} = 10 \times \dfrac{100/3}{250/3} = 4\ \text{V}$.

The absolute error in the measurement is $\Delta V = |V_{\text{measured}} - V_{\text{true}}| = |4 - 5| = 1\ \text{V}$.

The percentage error is $\dfrac{\Delta V}{V_{\text{true}}} \times 100\% = \dfrac{1}{5} \times 100\% = 20\%$.

Answer: $20\%$

103521.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When an electromagnetic wave travels from vacuum into a non-magnetic dielectric medium, its propagation speed ($E_0/B_0$) decreases but the ratio of electric field amplitude to magnetic intensity amplitude ($E_0/H_0$) increases.

Reason (R): For a non-magnetic dielectric medium, relative permeability is $1$ and relative permittivity is greater than $1$, making both $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu\varepsilon}}$ and $\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu}{\varepsilon}}$ smaller than their respective vacuum values.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
103521.sol:
The propagation speed of an electromagnetic wave is given by $v = \dfrac{E_0}{B_0} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu\varepsilon}}$.
The ratio of electric field amplitude to magnetic intensity amplitude (wave impedance) is given by $\dfrac{E_0}{H_0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\mu}{\varepsilon}}$.

For a non-magnetic dielectric medium, the relative permeability $\mu_r = 1$ (so $\mu = \mu_0$) and the relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r > 1$ (so $\varepsilon > \varepsilon_0$).

Substituting these values, the speed becomes $v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r}}$, which is less than the speed in vacuum ($c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}$). Thus, the propagation speed decreases.

Similarly, the ratio $\dfrac{E_0}{H_0}$ becomes $\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r}}$, which is less than the vacuum value ($\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon_0}}$). Thus, the ratio of electric field to magnetic intensity also decreases.

Therefore, the Assertion is incorrect because it states that the ratio $E_0/H_0$ increases. The Reason is correct as it accurately states that both quantities become smaller than their vacuum values.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

104496.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A fish in a pond looks at a bird flying vertically above in the air. To the fish, the bird appears to be at a greater height from the water surface than its actual height.
Reason (R): The apparent height $h'$ of an object at actual height $h$ in a rarer medium of refractive index $n_1$, when viewed from a denser medium of refractive index $n_2$, is given by $h' = h \left(\dfrac{n_1}{n_2}\right)$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
104496.sol:
Evaluate the Assertion (A):
When an object in a rarer medium (air) is viewed from a denser medium (water), the apparent height is given by $h' = h \times \dfrac{n_{\text{observer}}}{n_{\text{object}}}$.
Here, $n_{\text{observer}} = n_{\text{water}}$ and $n_{\text{object}} = n_{\text{air}}$. Since $n_{\text{water}} > n_{\text{air}}$, the apparent height $h'$ is greater than the actual height $h$. Thus, the bird appears to be at a greater height. The Assertion (A) is true.

Evaluate the Reason (R):
The general formula for apparent height/depth is $h' = h \left(\dfrac{n_{\text{observer}}}{n_{\text{object}}}\right)$.
In the given scenario, the observer is in the denser medium ($n_2$) and the object is in the rarer medium ($n_1$).
Therefore, the correct formula should be $h' = h \left(\dfrac{n_2}{n_1}\right)$.
The Reason states $h' = h \left(\dfrac{n_1}{n_2}\right)$, which is incorrect. The Reason (R) is false.

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

106446.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The shortest wavelength of the Paschen series for the $He^+$ ion is $\dfrac{9}{4R_H}$.
Statement II: In the photoelectric effect, the maximum kinetic energy of ejected electrons is independent of the frequency of incident light.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
106446.sol:
For Statement I: The Paschen series corresponds to $n_1 = 3$. The shortest wavelength corresponds to the maximum energy transition, which is the series limit ($n_2 = \infty$). For the $He^+$ ion, $Z = 2$.
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R_H Z^2 \left(\dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} ight)$
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R_H (2)^2 \left(\dfrac{1}{3^2} - \dfrac{1}{\infty} ight) = \dfrac{4R_H}{9}$
$\lambda = \dfrac{9}{4R_H}$
Thus, Statement I is true.

For Statement II: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, $K_{max} = h u - h u_0$. The maximum kinetic energy of ejected electrons depends linearly on the frequency of the incident light (for $ u > u_0$). It is independent of the intensity of light. Thus, Statement II is false.

Answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

Which of the following orders are correct against the property given? \(
(I)Dipole momentNF_3 > NH_3 > BF_3
(II)Covalent bond lengthC-O > N-O > O-H

\)

In \(\mathrm{NH}_3\), electronegativity of \(\mathrm{N}\)-atom is greater than \(\mathrm{H}\). Therefore, direction of all dipole moment with lone pairs lies in same direction, hence net dipole moment increases.
\(\mu_{\text{net }} \simeq 1.46 \mathrm{D}\)
In \(\mathrm{NF}_3\), electronegativity of \(\mathrm{F}\) is greater than \(\mathrm{N}\). Therefore, direction of dipole moment are opposite from the lone pair, hence, net dipole decreases.

(II) Covalent bond length
\(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O} > \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{O} > \mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\)
as electronegativity difference increases then bond length decreases but lone pair-lone pair repulsion increases the bond length.
(III) Bond order \(=\) Number of bonding electron \(\left(N_b\right)\)
\(\frac{- \text{ Number of antibonding electron }}{2}\)
\(\begin{gathered}
\mathrm{C}_2=\sigma 1 s^2 < \sigma^{\star} 1 s^2 < \sigma 2 s^2 < \sigma^* 2 s^2 < \pi 2 p_x^2 \simeq \pi 2 p_y^2 \\
\mathrm{BO}=\frac{8-4}{2}=2 \\
\mathrm{ B}_2=\sigma s^2 < \sigma^{\star} 1 s^2 < \sigma 2 s^2 < \sigma^{\star} 2 s^2 < \pi 2 p_x^1 \simeq \pi 2 p_y^1 \\
\mathrm{BO}=\frac{6-4}{2}=1 \\
\mathrm{He}_2=\sigma l s^2 < \sigma^* 1 s^2 \\
\mathrm{BO}=\frac{2-2}{2}=0 \text{ (does not exist.) }
\end{gathered}\)

107927.subject: Chemistry
107927.text: Which of the following does not have coordinate bond?
107927.sol:
A. $\mathrm{SO}_2$ (Sulfur Dioxide)
1. Sulfur has 6 valence electrons and each oxygen has 6 valence electrons.
2. In $\mathrm{SO}_2$, sulfur forms two double bonds with two oxygen atoms.
3. One of the oxygen atoms can donate a lone pair to sulfur, forming a coordinate bond.
4. Therefore, $\mathrm{SO}_2$ has a coordinate bond.
B. $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ (Nitric Acid)
1. Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons, each oxygen has 6, and hydrogen has 1.
2. In $\mathrm{HNO}_3$, nitrogen forms one double bond with one oxygen and single bonds with the other oxygen and hydrogen.
3. The nitrogen can use a lone pair to form a coordinate bond with one of the oxygens.
4. Therefore, $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ has a coordinate bond.
C. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_3$ (Sulfurous Acid)
1. Sulfur has 6 valence electrons, each oxygen has 6, and hydrogen has 1.
2. In $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_3$, sulfur forms two single bonds with two hydroxyl groups \((\mathrm{OH})\) and one double bond with an oxygen atom.
3. The sulfur can donate a lone pair to form a coordinate bond with the remaining oxygen.
4. Therefore, $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_3$ has a coordinate bond.
D. $\mathrm{HNO}_2$ (Nitrous Acid)
1. Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons, each oxygen has 6, and hydrogen has 1.
2. In HNO 2, nitrogen forms one double bond with one oxygen and a single bond with the hydroxyl group (OH).
3. The nitrogen does not have a lone pair available to donate to form a coordinate bond.
4. Therefore, $\mathrm{HNO}_2$ does not have a coordinate bond.
Conclusion
The compound that does not have a coordinate bond is $\mathrm{HNO}_2$.

108972.text: For a certain reversible chemical reaction, the equilibrium constants $K_c$ and $K_p$ are related as $\dfrac{K_c}{K_p} = (\mathrm{RT})^2$. Which of the following reactions satisfies this condition?
108972.sol:
The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is given by:
$K_p = K_c(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta n_g}$

Rearranging the given condition $\dfrac{K_c}{K_p} = (\mathrm{RT})^2$, we get:
$\dfrac{K_p}{K_c} = (\mathrm{RT})^{-2}$

Comparing this with the standard equation, we find $\Delta n_g = -2$.

Let us calculate $\Delta n_g$ (moles of gaseous products $-$ moles of gaseous reactants) for the given options:
1) $2\mathrm{NH}_{3(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$ : $\Delta n_g = (1 + 3) - 2 = +2$
2) $\mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_{3(\mathrm{g})}$ : $\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$
3) $\mathrm{PCl}_{5(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_{3(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{Cl}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$ : $\Delta n_g = (1 + 1) - 1 = +1$
4) $\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{I}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{HI}_{(\mathrm{g})}$ : $\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0$

Thus, the reaction $\mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_{3(\mathrm{g})}$ satisfies the given condition.

Answer: $\mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_{3(\mathrm{g})}$

113897.text:
Match the mixtures in List-I with their corresponding characteristics in List-II.

List-I (Mixture)List-II (Characteristic)
(A) $n$-Hexane + $n$-Heptane(I) Minimum boiling azeotrope
(B) Carbon disulfide + Acetone(II) Negative deviation from Raoult's law
(C) Phenol + Aniline(III) Positive deviation from Raoult's law
(D) Ethanol ($95\%$) + Water(IV) Obeys Raoult's law over entire concentration range

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
113897.sol:
(A) $n$-Hexane and $n$-Heptane have similar structures and intermolecular forces, so they form an ideal solution which obeys Raoult's law over the entire concentration range (IV).

(B) Carbon disulfide and acetone mixture shows a positive deviation from Raoult's law because the dipole-dipole interactions between solute and solvent are weaker than the interactions in pure components (III).

(C) Phenol and aniline form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds between the phenolic proton and the lone pair on the nitrogen atom of aniline. This leads to stronger A-B interactions than A-A or B-B, resulting in a negative deviation from Raoult's law (II).

(D) Ethanol ($95\%$) and water mixture shows a large positive deviation from Raoult's law and forms a minimum boiling azeotrope at this specific composition (I).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

119284.subject: Chemistry
119284.text: What is the major organic product formed when 2-(2-oxoethyl)cyclohexan-1-one is treated with $\text{NaBH}_4$ followed by heating with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$?
119284.sol:
$\text{NaBH}_4$ is a reducing agent that reduces both the ketone (in the ring) and the aldehyde (in the side chain) to secondary and primary alcohols, respectively. The intermediate formed is 2-(2-hydroxyethyl)cyclohexan-1-ol.

Heating with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ causes dehydration of both alcohol groups.

Dehydration follows Zaitsev's rule and favors the formation of the most stable, highly conjugated system.

Elimination of water from the ring and the side chain yields a conjugated diene. The double bond in the ring forms between C1 and C2, and the side chain forms a vinyl group, resulting in 1-vinylcyclohex-1-ene as the major thermodynamically stable product.

Answer: 1-Vinylcyclohex-1-ene

Answer: Hexanediamide

121744.subject: Botany
121744.text: What is the shape of the gametes in brown algae?
121744.sol: The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus. Sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous. Union of gametes may take place in water or within the oogonium (oogamous species). <mark>The gametes are pyriform (pear-shaped</mark>) and bear two laterally attached flagella. The common forms are Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus.

123239.subject: Botany
123239.text: Which type of cells in the mesophyll are elongated and arranged vertically?
123239.sol: The vertical section of a dorsiventral leaf through the lamina shows three main parts, namely, epidermis, mesophyll and vascular system. The epidermis which covers both the upper surface (adaxial epidermis) and lower surface (abaxial epidermis) of the leaf has a conspicuous cuticle. The abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis. The latter may even lack stomata. The tissue between the upper and the lower epidermis is called the mesophyll. Mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and carry out photosynthesis, is made up of parenchyma. It has two types of cells – the palisade parenchyma and the spongy parenchyma. The adaxially placed palisade parenchyma is made up of elongated cells, which are arranged vertically and parallel to each other. The oval or round and loosely arranged spongy parenchyma is situated below the palisade cells and extends to the lower epidermis. There are numerous large spaces and air cavities between these cells. Vascular system includes vascular bundles, which can be seen in the veins and the midrib. The size of the vascular bundles are dependent on the size of the veins. The veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of the dicot leaves. The vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thick walled bundle sheath cells. and find the position of xylem in the vascular bundle.

123757.subject: Botany
123757.text:
Condition of homologous chromosomesEvents during Prophase-I
A. Attraction between homologous chromosomes1. Crossing over
B. Exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes2. Synapsis
C. Repulsion between homologous chromosomes3. Segregation
D. Separation of homologous chromosomes4. Diplotene
123757.sol:
Synapsis is the process during the zygotene stage of prophase I where homologous chromosomes are attracted to each other and align along their entire lengths.
Crossing over occurs during the pachytene stage of prophase I. This is when non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes exchange genetic material, leading to genetic recombination.
During the Diplotene stage of prophase I, the synaptonemal complex begins to break down, leading to a slight repulsion between homologous chromosomes.
Segregation refers to the process that occurs during anaphase I of meiosis I, where homologous chromosomes are separated and pulled to opposite poles of the cell.

125790.text: How many microsporangia are in a typical anther?
125790.sol: If you were to collect a stamen each from ten flowers (each from different species) and arrange them on a slide, you would be able to appreciate the large variation in size seen in nature. A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed with each lobe having two theca, i.e., they are dithecous Often a longitudinal groove runs lengthwise separating the theca. Let us understand the various types of tissues and their organisation in the transverse section of an anther The bilobed nature of an anther is very distinct in the transverse section of the anther. The anther is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure consisting of four microsporangia located at the corners, two in each lobe. The microsporangia develop further and become pollen sacs.
